cls: Atypical (second-generation) antipsychotic - dopamine D2/D3 partial agonist
quick: Schizophrenia 1.5-6 mg once daily; bipolar mania 3-6 mg; bipolar/MDD adjunct depression 1.5-3 mg once daily
Take once daily with or without food
Risk of neonatal extrapyramidal/withdrawal symptoms in third trimester; use only if benefit outweighs risk
Limited data; consider drug benefit, infant exposure, and long half-life - caution
No adjustment for mild-moderate; not recommended in severe (CrCl <30)
No adjustment for mild-moderate; not recommended in severe hepatic impairment
Avoid - additive CNS depression and impaired judgment/motor skills
Metabolic parameters, weight, EPS/tardive dyskinesia, mood/suicidality, CBC
summary: Cariprazine is an atypical antipsychotic that acts as a partial agonist at dopamine D2 and especially D3 and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors, with 5-HT2A antagonism. It treats schizophrenia, bipolar I mania and depression, and is an adjunct for major depressive disorder. It has a boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis and for suicidal thoughts/behaviors. Its long half-life (and that of active metabolites) means effects and adverse reactions can appear or persist for weeks.
indications: Schizophrenia in adults and pediatric patients 13 years and older
Acute manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder in adults and pediatric patients 10 years and older
Depressive episodes of bipolar I disorder (bipolar depression) in adults
Adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults

dosage.d: Start 1.5 mg once daily; range 1.5-6 mg/day
Start 0.5 mg once daily; range 1.5-4.5 mg/day
Start 1.5 mg once daily; range 3-6 mg/day
Start 0.5 mg once daily; target 3 mg or 4.5 mg/day
Start 1.5 mg once daily; 1.5 mg or 3 mg/day
Start 1.5 mg once daily; 1.5 mg or 3 mg/day
Dose adjustment required (reduce dose per labeling)

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Because of the long half-life of cariprazine and its active metabolites, dose changes are not fully reflected in plasma for several weeks - titrate and assess slowly
Monitor for adverse reactions for several weeks after starting and after each dose change
Avoid concomitant strong CYP3A4 inducers; reduce dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
moa: The mechanism is not fully established, but efficacy is thought to result from partial agonism at dopamine D2 and D3 receptors (with notably high D3 affinity) and at serotonin 5-HT1A receptors, combined with antagonism at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. Partial agonism modulates dopaminergic transmission, reducing positive symptoms while limiting full dopamine blockade. Two long-acting active metabolites, desmethyl- and didesmethyl-cariprazine, contribute to sustained activity.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to cariprazine (reactions have included rash, urticaria, and angioedema)
relative: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (increased mortality - not approved)
Pre-existing low WBC / history of leukopenia or neutropenia
History of seizures, cardiovascular/cerebrovascular disease, or conditions predisposing to hypotension
monitor: CBC in patients with low baseline WBC

preg: Neonates exposed to antipsychotics in the third trimester are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms after delivery. Use cariprazine in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk; there is a pregnancy exposure registry for antipsychotics.
lact: There are no data on the presence of cariprazine in human milk or its effects on the breastfed infant. Given the long half-life, weigh developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against the infant's potential exposure and the mother's clinical need.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate renal impairment. Cariprazine is not recommended in patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) because it has not been evaluated.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate hepatic impairment. Cariprazine is not recommended in severe hepatic impairment as it has not been studied.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - increase cariprazine exposure; reduce dose
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, rifampin, St. John's wort) - reduce exposure; avoid (use not recommended)
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; avoid grapefruit (potential CYP3A4 inhibition)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid - additive central nervous system depression and impairment
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor fasting glucose, HbA1c, lipids, weight, and CBC

rare: Cerebrovascular events in elderly with dementia
emergency: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (hyperthermia, rigidity, autonomic instability)

monitoring: Weight, BMI, fasting glucose/HbA1c, and lipid profile at baseline and periodically
Complete blood count in patients with low baseline WBC
Mood, behavior, and suicidality (especially early and at dose changes)
counsel: Effects build up gradually because the drug stays in the body for weeks - keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not feel immediate change
Report uncontrolled movements, severe muscle stiffness with fever, or fainting
Watch for and report any worsening mood or thoughts of self-harm
Tell your doctor about all medicines - some seizure and antibiotic drugs interact
Avoid alcohol and rise slowly to prevent dizziness
Maintain a healthy diet and exercise; weight and blood sugar will be monitored
pk: Therapeutic effect develops gradually over days to weeks
Peak plasma concentration about 3-6 hours after dosing
Cariprazine about 2-4 days; active metabolite didesmethyl-cariprazine effective half-life 1-3 weeks
Prolonged - effects and adverse reactions can persist for weeks after stopping
Store at controlled room temperature 20-25 C
pearls: Boxed warnings: increased mortality in elderly dementia-related psychosis and suicidal thoughts/behaviors
Distinctly high affinity as a D3 partial agonist among antipsychotics
Very long-acting active metabolites mean dose changes take weeks to reach steady state - adjust slowly
Late-occurring adverse reactions can appear after starting because of the long half-life
Akathisia/EPS are among the most common reasons for dose adjustment
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose and resume the once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience. Possible effects include orthostatic hypotension, sedation, and extrapyramidal symptoms. Management is supportive: maintain airway/oxygenation, cardiovascular monitoring (continuous ECG for arrhythmias), and treatment of hypotension and EPS. There is no specific antidote; because of high protein binding and large volume of distribution, dialysis is unlikely to help. Effects may be prolonged owing to the long half-life.
